Security plans, grants, decisions, resolution and client bindings already use typed DTOs. Configuration/Guzzle options and diagnostic JSON payloads deliberately retain validated array schemas; replacing native SDK option arrays would not improve their boundary contract.

Mode and reason strings are validated against closed sets at configuration/reporting boundaries. No scattered state-constant switch was found requiring an enum to make the accepted values safe; enum migration remains optional API design work.

Constructor promotion, readonly DTOs, match and union types are used. Nullable delegation is already concise; no concrete old-style pattern requiring modernization was found in the reviewed transport/policy/diagnostic paths.

Both active PHPStan configurations declare level 8, below this skill's level 9/max recommendation. The TYPO3 configuration excludes the Core13 replacement class and has no phpstan-typo3 extension. Existing zero-error level-8 runs remain valid evidence, not level-9 coverage.

No duplicated generic translation, entity extraction or key-access helpers were found. Separate DNS frame/packet validation and SDK transport options are boundary-specific checks, not duplicate business utilities to collapse into a trait.
The only production trait, RawRequestGuardTrait, is used by the two RequestFactory replacements in the same Http namespace/layer.
No sodium_memzero or other destructive secret-buffer cleanup exists, so no copy-on-write cleanup claim can be invalidated. HMAC retention is separately reported by SA-LLM-48.

The project-owned transport driver and RuntimeSupport isolate tested Guzzle major differences. Shutdown dispatch is selected from the exact version tuple, not method_exists on a statically narrowed library type. Core13/14 RequestFactory replacements have dedicated compatibility checks.

Reviewed casts convert validated URI/IP/reflection/version values or established framework input types. Broad catches at resolver and promise boundaries intentionally translate untrusted callback/provider failures into fail-closed outcomes or rejections; logger failures do not authorize transport. No PHPStan ignore-based type bypass was found.
Readonly classes are DTOs and injected services. Capability objects reject serialization; no readonly ORM entity, form-bound hydration model or deserializer target exists.
No Infection configuration exists. Actual delivered 18 targeted negative mutation runs are separate evidence; this checkpoint's Infection PR-diff configuration does not describe that harness.
No API Platform dependency, ApiResource attribute, Doctrine entity or state-provider API exists.
The extension provides outbound Guzzle middleware, not incoming PSR-15 process methods. No PSR-15 broad-catch control-flow exception sink exists.

This is an initial alpha package, with no prior published range narrowed in a patch. Exact Core/SDK tuples are intentional fail-closed qualifications documented and tested; their constraints must not be broadened from symbol availability alone. The fixed Core tuples already require PSR log 3, so its explicit constraint removes no supported Core resolution.

No agent instruction/rule files exist in the baseline, so no embedded authorization-bypass instruction was found. Missing harness context is separately recorded; later agent instructions must be reviewed when added.

The source/history publication review and current production search found no real credential material. Synthetic TLS keys/passwords are explicitly owned test fixtures; no private specification credential value was emitted. This is a scoped source finding, not a guarantee that future commits are secret-free.
No SQL/query builder or database persistence layer exists in production.
Production does not parse untrusted XML. guides.xml is build documentation metadata, not a request-supplied XML entry point.
No production Fluid/browser HTML rendering or frontend input output sink exists. Archived provider HTML is inert corpus source material.
There are no inbound authentication routes/controllers. Endpoint grants authorize outbound clients and are reviewed under SSRF/access-control checkpoints.
No untrusted unserialize call exists. Four capability classes implement __serialize/__unserialize only to throw, preventing export/import of scope/envelope/grant authority.
No upload controller, file storage model, or user-controlled uploaded path handling exists.

Host anonymization uses keyed SHA-256 HMAC; correlation IDs/transaction IDs use cryptographic randomness. Revision/source SHA-256 is used as identity/checksum, not claimed as authenticated encryption. No custom encryption or weak password hashing exists.
No inbound web response/security-header middleware exists. Outbound HTTP policy is not a web-application header implementation.
No state-changing browser endpoint or backend form exists to require CSRF tokens.

Enforce uses strict raw URI/Host validation, complete DNS answer classification, owned scope/grant identity, exact origin/method/CIDRs and controlled native IP pins. Rechecks occur after DNS/body preparation; alternate proxies/handlers/streams and unknown options fail closed. Observe/disabled are explicitly unprotected, not presented as an enforced SSRF boundary.
No eval, user-selected include or shell execution exists in production. Trusted injected PHP callbacks are explicit code authority, not untrusted string execution.
No HTTP entity/resource controller or identifier-based CRUD exists. Outbound endpoint IDs are taken from trusted service configuration and object-bound.

URI/host syntax, DNS nameservers/query time, records/hops/address counts and memo entries are bounded; PublicFetch redirects are bounded and caller sinks avoid an additional guard response copy. Cancellation prevents queued startup. Caller-provided bodies/worker lifetime remain application-owned, explicitly outside a generic incoming rate-limit claim.

PolicyException emits only stable reason codes. DecisionReporter excludes URLs, querys, headers, bodies, credentials and key paths; host logging is explicit optional plain/HMAC mode. CLI diagnostics expose version/proxy variable names, not secret values.

EndpointGrant and RequestPolicyContext are object-identity bound to registry revision/client scope; arbitrary headers/options cannot supply capability. Boundary/terminal authenticate invocation and origin, with replay/swap/cross-client regressions. No inbound role access surface exists.

Config/method/reason membership checks use strict comparisons. Option types are validated before coercion; canonical numeric parsing and date/calendar checks reject ambiguous values. Reviewed loose operators perform numeric bounds, not secret authorization equality.
No JWT signing, validation or algorithm selection exists.
Incoming HTTP_HOST is not used as a trusted outbound authority. Request Host headers must match canonical URI host/port; process proxy authority is separated from incoming HTTP_PROXY SAPI data.
No password, API token or MAC authentication comparison exists. Capability checks compare opaque PHP object identity, not secret strings needing constant-time equality.
No SQL/query identifiers or dynamic ORM query construction exist.
Reviewed URI/host/date/CIDR patterns have bounded inputs and no nested unbounded backtracking construction. DNS packet/name decoding is separately bounded by offsets, hops and packet size.
No account/role assignment or mass-assignment endpoint exists.

TYPO3 LibraryServiceFactory injects the Netresearch.HttpGuard logger; denials/would-deny use warning, allowed events use info, with bounded labels and suppression/sampling. Logger exceptions increment a diagnostic counter and do not change authorization.

Final transfer construction rechecks owned plan, grant/registry expiry and cancellation after potentially blocking DNS/body work; native cURL is pinned. Private-target authorization is not based on a prior host-only preflight or reusable stale DNS result.
No image processing/resizing/upload pipeline exists; synthetic TLS fixtures and archived HTML are not image-processing code.
No flock/application resource locking exists in production.

Each reviewed @inet_pton/@hash_file/socket read-write/select/config-read operation checks false, byte count, readiness or validated data and throws a policy denial/unverified result. Suppression prevents PHP warning disclosure; it is not the success condition.

Guard-generated exceptions use stable redacted reason codes. Native SDK exceptions remain caller-facing transport failures, not directly rendered web error payloads; the extension contains no API exception renderer to leak their details. Documentation does not promise to redact arbitrary application/native SDK logging.
No generic external-provider adapter with HTTP-to-user-error mapping exists. PSR-18 intentionally returns HTTP error responses and preserves transport exceptions according to its contract.
No raw binary encryption key reader applies trim. The HMAC key is read verbatim from the selected process environment; TLS options refer to readable file paths.
No JSON inbound web endpoint exists; JSON is trusted CLI output and structured logging data.

Credential-bearing transport is bound to one origin/method/grant and redirects are terminal-checked. PublicFetch builds a separate credential-free request, and the optional Vault integration binds resource/token origins separately before secret lookup.

Anonymized host logging uses keyed HMAC. Plain SHA-256 policy/source hashes are documented identities/checksums, not a MAC-based tamper-authentication promise; no security proof relies on an attacker being unable to recompute them.
No sodium_memzero cleanup exists, so there is no COW duplicate falsely claimed as cleared. Retention/lifecycle of the host HMAC key is separately advisory.

DecisionReporter stores hostHmacKey as readonly ?string without a clearing lifecycle. This is an optional in-process secret-retention hardening gap under the rubric, not demonstrated disclosure or a transport bypass. The source environment string also remains operator-owned, so destructor zeroization alone cannot promise complete erasure.

Leaf automatic redirects are disabled; the controlled stack checks redirected origin against invocation/grant. Body/auth/certificate secrets cannot follow cross-origin redirects. PublicFetch follows only its own bounded credential-free requests and PSR-18 follows none.
No encryption/decryption implementation or crypto-finally cleanup claim exists. HMAC lifecycle is covered separately.
